definition.method: Execute a comparative policy divergence study across two distinct training horizons (10k vs 200k episodes) in a deterministic gridworld to determine if initial path divergence converges (transient) or maintains significance (stable).
definition.stop: If late-phase divergence measures consistently below 0.05, interpret as transient variance and close current hypothesis testing.
definition.success: Evidence of sustained policy divergence (>0.15) at late-phase suggests path-dependent preference formation is not merely transient noise.

proposal.summary: This cycle refines the investigation into path-dependent preference formation by introducing a differential measurement protocol to distinguish between transient state variance and stable preference emergence in reinforcement learning agents. This builds upon the inconclusive findings from exp-mem-pref-08 by comparing policy divergence across different training horizons.
proposal.title: Refining Stability Analysis in Preference Formation
